title: QBR health + renewal KPI cheat-sheet and tracker template
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact, reproducible cheat-sheet to drive QBR conversations and renewal health scoring for accounts using Redwood inference. It focuses on the operational KPIs we care about (latency, uptime, cost-per-token, cache hit rate) and provides: definitions, measurement windows, threshold buckets, recommended talking points for QBRs, and a simple renewal tracker table you can copy into spreadsheets.

Version notes / context:
- Draft for CS reps and solutions engineers preparing QBRs for hosted & dedicated customers.
- Lean, actionable: use this for slide speaker notes and for the renewal playbook check before account review.
- Open questions at the end — please add observed edge cases after QBRs.

Metric definitions and measurement rules:
1) P50 / P95 / P99 Latency (ms)
   - Definition: end-to-end server-side generation latency measured from API request accept time to final token delivery (server-side processing only). Excludes network RTT and client-side parsing.
   - Measurement window: 30-day rolling; report both 7-day trend and 30-day aggregate in QBR.
   - Calculation notes: compute percentiles on per-request medians (not token-level). For streaming flows, measure time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and total completion; include both in notes.

2) Uptime (availability)
   - Definition: percentage of customer API requests that received a 2xx response within configured SLA window in the reporting period.
   - Measurement window: calendar quarter (primary) and last 30 days (operational).
   - Exclusions: planned maintenance windows and agreed emergency maintenance (must be documented).

3) Cost-per-token (USD/token)
   - Definition: average billed cost divided by total billed output tokens for the account over the window. For multi-model setups, show per-model cost if one model is >20% of spend.
   - Measurement window: rolling 30-day and quarter-to-date.
   - Notes: include caching and batching savings as separate lines so customers can see raw vs effective cost.

4) Cache Hit Rate (prefix / KV cache)
   - Definition: percent of requests that were served (fully or partially) from server-side KV/prefix cache such that token compute was avoided for cached segments.
   - Measurement window: 30-day rolling.
   - Notes: show absolute hits and hit efficiency (saved tokens / total tokens).

Derived KPI: Renewal Health Score
   - Purpose: single-number snapshot to prioritize renewal outreach and playbook actions.
   - Lightweight formula (suggested):
     Renewal Health = (0.25 * LatencyScore) + (0.30 * UptimeScore) + (0.25 * CostScore) + (0.20 * CacheScore)
   - Per-metric scoring: map metric into 0-100 where higher is better. Example mapping (customize per account):
       LatencyScore: 100 if P95 < 250ms, 75 if P95 250-500ms, 40 if 500-1000ms, 0 if >1000ms
       UptimeScore: 100 if >= 99.95%, 80 if 99.9-99.95, 50 if 99-99.9, 0 if <99%
       CostScore: 100 if cost/token <= target_by_tier, 70 if <= 1.5x target, 30 if 1.5-3x, 0 if >3x
       CacheScore: 100 if hit rate >= 40%, 70 if 20-40%, 30 if 5-20%, 0 if <5%
   - Output bands: 85-100 green (healthy renew), 60-85 yellow (engage for optimization), <60 red (risk — immediate playbook).

QBR KPI table (copyable ASCII table for slides and spreadsheets):

| KPI                | Window     | Value (example) | Target (recommended) | Action if missed | Notes |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------|----------------------|------------------|-------|
| P95 latency (ms)   | 30-day     | 340             | <250                 | SE tuning + route policy | streaming delays on long sequences |
| Uptime (%)         | Quarter    | 99.88           | >=99.95              | Incident review + SRE runbook | maintenance excluded |
| Cost / token (USD) | 30-day     | 0.0038          | 0.0025 (tier A)      | Quantize + batching review | includes caching savings |
| Cache hit rate (%)  | 30-day     | 18              | >=40%                | Prompt engineering + SDK caching hints | low reuse for chat flows |

Actionable playbook snippets (quick)
- If Renewal Health < 60 (red): schedule joint SE deep-dive within 7 business days. Topics: model choice, quantization, batch config, routing policy, cache keys. Open a joint Jira for prioritized fixes.
- If CostScore low (>1.5x target): propose immediate pilot of 8-bit quantized model variant and 1-week rerun of high-volume prompt set to measure savings.
- If LatencyScore low and P95 driven by large seq lengths: recommend prefix caching where feasible and shorter max tokens on interactive routes.
- If Uptime issues: escalate to SRE; provide RCA and interim routing fallback to dedicated pool or different region.

Renewal tracker template (one-line copy to paste into Sheets)
Columns: Account / ARR band / Renewal date / Renewal Health (0-100) / Latency (P95 ms) / Uptime (%) / Cost/token (USD) / Cache hit rate (%) / Next action / Owner / Notes / Jira link
Sample row (comma-separated for quick paste):
Acme Corp, $180K, 2025-06-30, 57, 520, 99.72, 0.0046, 9, SE deep-dive scheduled, Asha Patel, JIRA-ACME-788

QBR talking points template (speaker bullets)
- Quick health snapshot: Renewal Health X (band) + top metric driver.
- Wins since last QBR: e.g., cost reduced 12% after scaled batching change.
- Risks & mitigations: specific item (latency spike on X route) + action owner and ETA.
- Opportunity: proposed optimization (quantized variant pilot) and expected uplift/cost delta.
- Ask: technical decision needed or access required (e.g., enable KV caching, provide prompt sets).

Open questions / TODOs (please edit)
- Agree on canonical measurement windows for renewal scoring across hosted vs dedicated (does dedicated exclude certain infra incidents?).
- Finalize cost-per-token tier thresholds by ARR band (finance input needed).
- Add an automated export of these four KPIs to the CS dashboard (engineering ticket referenced above).

Appendix: quick calculation examples
- Effective cost-with-cache = billed_cost / (total_output_tokens - saved_tokens_from_cache) 
- Cache hit rate = hits / total_requests (or saved_tokens / total_output_tokens for token-weighted view)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive so CS can standardize QBRs and renewal prioritization.
- After first 10 customer pilots, we'll re-calibrate weightings and thresholds.

Contact: Asha Patel (asha@redwood.ai) — add notes back into this doc after live QBRs.
